title.narrative: UNFPA Sexual and reproductive health and rights 2017-2020
UNFPA Sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter 2017-2020

description.narrative: The objectives of the UNFPA country programme for Ethiopia 2016-2020 focus on: SRHR (including HIV), adolescents and youth, gender equality and women’s economic empowerment, and population dynamics. However, due to the spread of Covid-19 in Ethiopia, and the already noted and further expected negative consequences of the pandemic in terms of limiting access to SRHR, increasing GBV, and, placing a very heavy burden on the national health system, additional objectives for 2020 are included: -Ensuring continuity of access to SRHR services during the Covid-19 pandemic. -Addressing GBV, including strengthening health facilities and safe houses and access to them. -Ensuring a continuous supply of contraceptives and reproductive health services. -Promoting youth engagement for SRHR, and ‘leaving no one behind’. Promoting communication on risks due to Covid-19, and community engagement.

Insatsen är ett stöd till UNFPAs landprogram i Etiopien 2017-2020 för deras arbete med sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter, och genom avtalsändringen planerar Sverige att tillföra medel för att bidra till UNFPA:s respons på Covid-19 epedemin i Etiopien.

This contribution is a support to UNFPA's country programme in Ethiopia 2017-2020, with the aim to strengthen access and quality of sexual and reproductive health and rights, and through an amendment to the agreement Sweden is planning to add funds for 2020 in order to scale up the contribution to the UNFPA:s response to Covid-19.

Overall this contribution has successfully assisted to ensure access to SRHR across the Ethiopian regions and to reach the most vulnerable in particular, especially youth and women, but also amongst IDPs and refugees. The contribution has also placed special emphasis on the continued access to SRHR under the pandemic, and the following important results were reported from UNFPA up to December 2020, as part of the Covid-19 response: training of 643 health workers trained on Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Reponse (MPDSR) and Emergency Bbstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC), 436 health workers trained on COVID-adapted SRHR services, 800 communities having made declarations against FGM/child marriage, 16 210 girls and boys survivors of GBV treated and got psychosocial and juridical support, and 4 733 women treated for fistula (116 treated January-June 2020).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
